subject: Order form - price band offsets & packaging definitions (redline questions)
messages:
From: Sarah Gomez <sarah.gomez@acmecloud.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Cc: AcmeCloud Procurement <procurement@acmecloud.com>
Date: Thu, 28 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Questions on order form price bands and packaging

Hi Priyom,

Thanks for sending over the draft order form. Our procurement and finance teams reviewed the pricing exhibit and came back with a few items that need clarification before we can circulate to legal. I've attached our annotated redline (ACME_Redline_v1.pdf). High-level questions below: 

1) Billing slab "offset" behavior: does the slab offset apply only to committed usage (monthly committed tokens) or does it net against burst/overage as well? Concern: if reserved credits reduce committed usage but we burst, will true-ups be larger than expected?

2) Packaging definition ambiguity: the order form references "bundled features" and "add-on SKUs" in the same section. We need a clear, operational definition that billing can use — what counts as a pack vs. an add-on for minimum-commit calculations?

3) Cap/floor interactions: Exhibit B's floor language plus the pricing cap for certain GPU-backed instances seems to create a scenario where the floor count triggers a clawback even when actual spend is within a capped rate. Can you confirm intended remedy waterfall?

We want to avoid a surprise true-up for Q1 after go-live. Can we get a short write-up on your intended mechanics and any proposed mitigation (e.g., first-quarter pro-rate buffer or grace band)?

Available this week for a 30-min call; prefer Thu morning PT.

Thanks,
Sarah Gomez
Sr. Procurement Manager | AcmeCloud
Attachments: ACME_Redline_v1.pdf (annotated order form)

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Gomez <sarah.gomez@acmecloud.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 29 May 2026 10:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Questions on order form price bands and packaging

Sarah — thanks for the clear notes and the annotated PDF. I read through the ACME_Redline_v1 and pulled the key operating questions into the bullets below so we can be explicit. Copying legal and finance to capture redline language.

Quick answers (longer clarifications below):
- Billing slab offsets: intended to apply to committed usage only — burst/overage billed at the applicable overage rate and not offset by committed credits.
- Packaging: propose a short definition: "bundled features" are SKUs included in a named package on the order schedule; "add-on SKUs" are optional line items not counted toward minimum commit unless explicitly listed as committed.
- Cap/floor waterfall: agree we need to tighten language so the floor true-up does not double-count capped-rate adjustments. We'll propose tightened Exhibit B language.

I've attached our internal redline (PR_Redline_v2.pdf) with suggested replacement language and an operational note for billing. Two asks: (1) can you confirm that the proposed packaging definition covers your use cases, and (2) do you want Redwood to apply a one-quarter buffer (pro-rated 10% protection) on any floor true-ups for the first billing period post-go-live? If yes we'll reflect it in the redline.

Proposed call: Thu 4 Jun 2026 9:30 AM PT — listed as 30 minutes. If that's tight for you, let me know a couple of alternatives.

Thanks — talk soon.
Priyom Das
Senior Manager, Sales Operations | Redwood Inference
Attachments: PR_Redline_v2.pdf

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Sarah Gomez <sarah.gomez@acmecloud.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Jun 2026 11:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Order form - legal redlines and recommended clause language

Sarah / Priyom — I reviewed ACME_Redline_v1 and PR_Redline_v2 and prepared a short set of legal recommendations (see attached OF_Sched_Annex_Markup.docx). Key points summarized here to speed alignment before the call: 

1) Billing slab offset (recommended language): add clause to Exhibit A: "Committed Credits shall only offset charges invoiced under the Committed Usage Schedule. Any usage billed as Overage or Burst shall be invoiced at the rates set forth in the Overage Rate Table and shall not be reduced by Committed Credits." This makes the mechanics explicit.

2) Packaging and minimum-commit definitions: replace the phrase "bundled features" with a defined term in Exhibit C: "'Package' means a set of SKUs explicitly enumerated on the Order Schedule and designated as included in Customer's Minimum Commitment. 'Add-on' means any SKU listed as optional in the Order Schedule and expressly excluded from Minimum Commitment calculations." This resolves billing ambiguity.

3) Cap/floor interplay and remedy waterfall: concern noted about double counting. Proposed approach: (a) apply capped unit rates when computing billed charges; (b) compute floor true-up against the net effective billed amount after application of caps; (c) provide a one-quarter 'first-bill buffer' where the Floor True-Up will be reduced by a percentage (10%) for the first full billing period following go-live, subject to reconciliation at the first annual true-up.

4) Operational note for billing: include an appendix with worked examples (three rows: normal, burst, and reserved-credit offset) to ensure finance systems implement the same sequence of operations.

If Acme accepts points 1–3 we can fold language into the order form and provide a tracked PDF. I suggest we avoid open-ended 'grace period' language; stick to a single, timeboxed buffer.

Attachment: OF_Sched_Annex_Markup.docx (redline + example worksheet)

-Karthik
General Counsel (Contracts) | Redwood Inference

That buffer will be shown as an adjustment on the invoice and reconciled at the first annual true-up. If acceptable we'll insert the sentence into Exhibit B and reflect in the billing examples appendix.
